adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation in admin-group.js.es6 (Math.floor + 1) creates a phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil with a zero guard
Template group_member.hbs resolves 'automatic' against the member context instead of the group, so the remove button renders for members of automatic groups
removeMember has no error handling, so a rejected DELETE on an automatic group gives the admin no feedback
create action in admin/groups_controller.rb silently drops the alias_level parameter, causing silent loss of user input on group creation

adjudication.rationale: In the new client code, `Discourse.Group#create()` POSTs `this.asJSON()` which includes `{ name, alias_level, visible }`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]` (or any alias_level param). As a result, any alias level selected in the UI during group creation will be ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias_level, i.e., silent loss of user input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing GroupUser callbacks and leaving the user_count counter cache stale on the group record

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff changes member removal to `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `group.save`. Unlike the add path (`group.add(user)`) and the previous code path (`group.remove(user)`), this direct association delete does not update any of the group’s own bookkeeping in this method (e.g., `user_count`). Since the UI and pagination logic added in the diff relies on `user_count` (e.g., `totalPages`, `next`/`previous`, and `{{user_count}}` in the template), a removal that doesn’t trigger the same membership/counter update mechanism can leave `user_count` stale. Using `delete` on an association also bypasses join-model destroy callbacks (where counter caches are typically maintained), making this a concrete correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for remove_member only asserts users.count, so the stale user_count regression would not be caught

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding is about test coverage (an assertion that would fail to catch a hypothetical future regression) rather than a concrete defect introduced by this diff. In the implementation, the members endpoint returns `meta.total` computed from `group.users.count`, and the client updates `user_count` from that meta in `findMembers()`. After `removeMember`, the client explicitly calls `findMembers()` again, which would refresh `user_count`. Also, the diff snippet of the `remove_member` spec is truncated, so the claim about what it asserts is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember refetches with the unchanged offset after removal, so removing the last member of the last page leaves an empty page with totalPages/currentPage desync

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `removeMember` (in `discourse/models/group.js`) does a DELETE then immediately calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. `findMembers()` clamps `offset` using the *current* `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`), but `user_count` has not been decremented yet (it only updates from the AJAX response). If you remove the last user on the last page, the old `offset` can now be equal to or greater than the new total, and the server (`GroupsController#members`) applies `offset(offset)` as-is, returning an empty `members` array. The client then sets `members: []` while still on that page, yielding an empty page state. Additionally, the controller’s `totalPages` computation (`Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`) will report 2 pages for exactly 50 users with limit 50, exacerbating page/page-count inconsistency after removals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers has no request cancellation or serialization, so out-of-order pagination responses can overwrite newer state and desync members/offset
All membership failure paths (removeMember, addMembers, findMembers) are swallowed with no .catch/.fail, so the UI shows success on failure and a failed fetch is indistinguishable from no members
add_members silently skips unknown usernames and still returns success_json, giving no indication a member was not added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record. Unknown usernames are simply skipped (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`) with no error collected. After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if successful, renders `success_json` regardless of whether any requested usernames were actually added. This means a request containing nonexistent usernames can return success with no indication that some (or all) additions were ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The usernames input is not cleared after adding members (in-code TODO), so re-clicking Add silently re-submits the same list

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `usernames` afterward. The template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, so the entered usernames remain in the field. Clicking the Add button again will invoke `addMembers` again and re-submit the same `usernames` string to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Automatic-group membership test uses xhr :put instead of xhr :delete for the remove_member route, failing to exercise the real DELETE route and masking routing regressions
Unbounded limit parameter in groups_controller#members allows any caller to request ?limit=99999999, forcing full materialization and serialization of all group members

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` without any upper bound. A caller who can hit this endpoint (subject to `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`) can supply an arbitrarily large `?limit=` value, causing the server to query and serialize a very large number of users in one request (potentially the entire group), creating a clear performance/DoS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query shape in admin groups_controller#add_members: one User.find_by_username query plus group.add triggers per username in a loop

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the diff adds a loop over `usernames.split(",")` that calls `User.find_by_username(username)` for each username and then `group.add(user)`. This produces one DB lookup per username (and potentially additional per-user work inside `group.add`), which is a classic N+1 query/per-item operation pattern and is directly verifiable from the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on the number of usernames accepted per request in add_members, allowing thousands of sequential queries and inserts in a single request

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` takes `params[:usernames]`, does `usernames.split(",").each`, and for each entry performs `User.find_by_username` (potentially one DB query per username) plus `group.add(user)` (likely insert per user) before a final `group.save`. There is no validation or cap on how many usernames can be provided, so a single request can trigger thousands of sequential lookups/inserts and tie up the request thread. This is directly verifiable from the added controller action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController#index serializes every group with no pagination, with per-row user_count aggregation and no limit on the groups table

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#index the code still does `groups = Group.order(:name)` (optionally filtered) and then `render_serialized(groups, BasicGroupSerializer)` with no pagination/limit, so it will serialize all matching groups. However, the finding’s claim about “per-row user_count aggregation” is not verifiable from this diff: we don’t see BasicGroupSerializer’s implementation, and `user_count` could be a counter-cache column rather than an aggregated query per row. Also, this behavior is not introduced by the diff (only a minor `ilike` -> `ILIKE` change), so the finding overstates what can be confirmed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from top-level array to {members, meta} envelope, breaking existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the response changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns a top-level JSON array of members) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, i.e., an envelope object. The frontend is updated accordingly (`group.js` now expects `result.members` and `result.meta`), but any existing external consumers calling `GET /groups/:name/members` and expecting an array will break due to the incompatible response shape change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update endpoint PUT /admin/groups/:id changed from nested params[:group] to flat params, silently dropping old clients' fields and silently flipping visible to false when params[:visible] is nil

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the code was changed from reading `payload = params[:group]` and then using `payload[:...]` to reading flat `params[:...]` directly. Old clients that still send `group: { ... }` will now have `params[:visible]`/`params[:alias_level]`/`params[:name]` unset, so those fields are ignored. Worse, `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to `false` whenever `params[:visible]` is nil (e.g., when the client sends only `params[:group][:visible]`), causing a silent flip to false. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update endpoint no longer handles params[:group][:usernames], silently dropping membership updates with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#update was changed from reading a nested payload = params[:group] (including payload[:usernames] to update membership) to reading only top-level params (:alias_level, :visible, :name). There is no handling of params[:group][:usernames] anymore, and the action will still return success_json (HTTP 200) as long as group.save succeeds, effectively ignoring any submitted usernames/membership changes. Membership updates were moved to new add_members/remove_member endpoints, but the update endpoint itself would now silently drop the old usernames payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH /admin/groups/:id incremental membership API (changes: {add, delete}) removed entirely; PATCH now falls into update and silently does nothing instead of returning 404/410

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#update no longer branches on request.patch? and the old update_patch method (handling params[:changes] with add/delete membership) is removed. Routes/tests for incremental PATCH membership are also removed, replaced by PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members. As a result, a PATCH to /admin/groups/:id that previously adjusted membership via changes:{add,delete} will now be routed to #update, ignore params[:changes], and typically still return success_json after group.save (i.e., no membership change and no error).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin GET /admin/groups/:id/users route deleted without replacement or deprecation, causing routing errors for consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` route under `namespace :admin do resources :groups`, but it is replaced by other endpoints: member listing now comes from the non-admin `/groups/:group_id/members.json` (updated `GroupsController#members` and `Group.findMembers()`), and admin membership modification is provided via new `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`. There are no remaining references in the diff to `/admin/groups/:id/users`, so the claim that this deletion will cause routing errors is not verifiable from the changes shown and the “without replacement” part is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin create endpoint POST /admin/groups changed from nested group payload to flat params and dropped usernames support; old clients sending group[name] produce empty-name validation failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create to read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible]) instead of the prior nested payload (params[:group][:name], params[:group][:usernames]). If a client still POSTs {group: {name: ...}}, then params[:name] is nil and the code sets group.name to '' ("(params[:name] || '').strip"), which will fail validations and return an error. It also removes setting usernames during create, so old clients relying on create-with-usernames will no longer add members. This behavior change is directly evidenced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces a blank trailing page in admin group UI when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same off-by-one pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields an extra trailing/blank page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint now truncates non-automatic groups at default limit of 50 (previously returned all members), with no upper bound on params[:limit] for large values

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the old code returned **all** members for non-automatic groups (no `limit/offset` applied), and only paginated automatic groups (default limit 200). The new code applies pagination to **all** groups with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so non-automatic groups will now return only 50 members by default unless the client supplies a larger `limit`. Also, there is no cap/sanity check on `params[:limit]`, so a request can set an arbitrarily large limit, potentially causing expensive queries/serialization on a public endpoint guarded only by `ensure_can_see!`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint accepts negative offset, generating OFFSET -1 which raises a PG::Error (500) in PostgreSQL

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the new code does `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then unconditionally applies it via `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamp/validation to prevent negative values. If a client supplies `?offset=-1`, Rails will pass `OFFSET -1` to PostgreSQL, which rejects negative OFFSET and can raise a PG error (resulting in a 500). The frontend model clamps offset to >= 0, but the public endpoint itself remains vulnerable to direct requests with negative offsets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test uses xhr :put for remove_member, routing to add_members instead, so the remove_member automatic-group guard is untested with false coverage

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin members endpoints are defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, so `remove_member` is only reachable via DELETE in real routing. But in the spec (context ".remove_member") the test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which uses the wrong HTTP verb and therefore doesn’t reflect the real route (a real PUT to `/admin/groups/:id/members` would go to `add_members`). This is a verifiable mismatch that can give misleading test coverage of the endpoint behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember() and addMembers() AJAX calls have no .catch()/rejection handler, so 422/500/network failures are completely silent and the admin believes the operation succeeded

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Discourse.Group#addMembers` and `#removeMember` call `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without any explicit `.catch()`/rejection handling, and the controller actions (`addMembers`, `removeMember`) also don’t attach handlers. However, the proposed finding’s key claim (“422/500/network failures are completely silent and the admin believes the operation succeeded”) is not directly verifiable from this diff: there is no success UI/flash being shown here, and whether failures are “silent” depends on existing global `Discourse.ajax`/AJAX error handling elsewhere (not shown in the diff). Therefore the finding overstates a non-verifiable behavior based solely on this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers() in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 has no error handling, so a failed members request silently renders an empty member list with no error state

adjudication.rationale: In both routes, the diff changes from returning the `model.findMembers()` promise in `afterModel` to calling `model.findMembers()` inside `setupController` without returning it or attaching any `.catch`/error action. As a result, if the `/groups/:name/members.json` request fails, the route transition won't enter Ember's error substates (because the hook isn't waiting on the promise), and there is no local error handling to set an error state. The template will simply render with `members` undefined/stale (effectively empty) and no explicit error UI from this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, producing a phantom empty page

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` when `user_count > 0`. If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 even though there is only 1 page. This also interacts with `next`, which can set `offset` to `user_count`, causing `findMembers()` to request an empty page and display `currentPage`/`totalPages` as the extra page. The correct logic should be closer to `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero case handled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server add_members reports success even when zero members were added, since nonexistent or whitespace-padded usernames (no .strip) are silently skipped

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. This means inputs like "bob, alice" will attempt to look up " alice" and silently skip it. Also, if all provided usernames are nonexistent (or whitespace-padded), the loop adds no users, but `group.save` will still typically succeed and the action renders `success_json`, so the endpoint reports success even though zero members were added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller update endpoint reads top-level params instead of the old nested params[:group], and group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" runs unconditionally, silently flipping visible to false for existing API consumers sending the old payload shape

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the diff changes from reading a nested payload (`payload = params[:group]`) to reading top-level params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`). It also sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. For existing clients still sending the old shape (e.g. `group: { visible: "true" }`), `params[:visible]` will be nil, so `nil == "true"` becomes false and `visible` will be silently flipped off. This is a concrete backward-compatibility/correctness regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers has no in-flight guard, request cancellation, or sequence token, so rapid pagination clicks allow stale out-of-order responses to overwrite offset/user_count/members state
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: findMembers is asynchronous and its results aren’t coordinated/handled safely, leading to race conditions where responses can arrive out of order and update controller state before/after expected timing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller members endpoint passes unvalidated negative offset directly into ActiveRecord's offset(), causing a PostgreSQL error and 500, and there is no upper clamp on limit

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members` (diff shows it rewritten), `offset = params[:offset].to_i` is passed directly into `group.users...offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. A negative `offset` (e.g. `?offset=-10`) will be sent to SQL as `OFFSET -10`, which PostgreSQL rejects (“OFFSET must not be negative”), causing a server error. Similarly, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in `.limit(limit)` with no upper bound, so a very large `limit` can be requested (performance/DoS risk). Although the JS client clamps offset, the server endpoint itself does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers button has no double-submit protection and the input is never cleared, allowing rapid clicks to fire multiple redundant PUT requests

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action only checks `Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))` and then immediately calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` with no state change (no disabling of the button, no in-flight flag) and no `.then(...)` handling. In the template `group.hbs`, the Add button (`<button {{action "addMembers"}} ...>`) is not bound to any `disabled` condition. As a result, rapid repeated clicks will trigger multiple PUT requests to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`. Also, the code contains a TODO "should clear the input" and never resets `usernames` after adding, so the input value remains and can be resent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a resolved promise on the empty-name path, so any caller chaining .then() will get a TypeError
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that a code path in the function fails to explicitly return a value, causing the function to yield undefined. The candidate frames it specifically as returning undefined instead of a (resolved) promise on an empty-name branch, which is a direct instance of the golden issue (missing return on some paths).

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put while the route is delete "members", so the test does not verify the DELETE route is actually wired and a routing regression would go undetected
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the remove_member spec uses xhr :put while the route is defined as a DELETE to groups#remove_member, meaning the test isn't exercising the correct HTTP verb/route wiring. This is the same mismatch described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 returns incorrect page count for user_counts that are exact multiples of limit (e.g., 100/50 returns 3 instead of 2), leaving next-page link enabled and causing phantom empty page

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (unless user_count == 0). For exact multiples of limit (e.g. user_count=100, limit=50), this yields 3 instead of the correct 2 (should be `Math.ceil(...)`). This makes `showingLast` false on page 2, enabling the "next" action. The `next` action then sets offset to `min(offset+limit, user_count)` which becomes 100, and Group.findMembers requests offset=100, returning an empty members list—i.e., a phantom empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No frontend tests exist for the new pagination logic (currentPage, totalPages, next/previous clamping) in admin-group.js.es6

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new frontend pagination/computed logic in `admin-group.js.es6` (`currentPage`, `totalPages`, `showingFirst`, `showingLast`, and `next`/`previous` actions with clamping), but the only tests added/modified in this diff are Ruby controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`). There are no added/updated JS/QUnit/Ember frontend tests covering this new pagination behavior, so the finding is verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec coverage for the changed /groups/:id/members response format in groups_controller.rb, which now returns a {members, meta:{total, limit, offset}} envelope instead of a serialized array

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (array response) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (enveloped response). However, the proposed finding claims there is *no spec coverage* for this change, which is not verifiable from the diff alone: the diff does not show any `groups_controller_spec` files (only `admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`), and a test for `/groups/:id/members` could exist elsewhere outside the shown changes. So while the response format change is real, the asserted lack of spec coverage is not conclusively demonstrated by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination is now applied to all groups in groups_controller.rb members action, whereas previously only automatic groups were paginated — behavior change is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from returning the full member list for non-automatic groups (pagination only applied inside `if group.automatic?`) to always applying `limit`/`offset` (default `limit` 50) and returning a new JSON shape `{members: ..., meta: ...}`. That is a verifiable behavior change affecting all groups, not just automatic ones, and the diff does not add/adjust any specs for `GroupsController#members` to cover this new paginated behavior/response format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default member limit changed from 200 to 50 without test verification

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the default `limit` in `GroupsController#members` from a previous implicit/conditional behavior (200 only for automatic groups; otherwise effectively unbounded) to `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` for all groups. However, this is paired with a new pagination implementation on the client (`limit/offset`, next/previous actions, `totalPages`, etc.) and server now returns `meta.total/limit/offset`, indicating the change is intentional rather than a defect. The claim “without test verification” is also not a verifiable bug by itself—tests for the members limit behavior weren’t shown before either, and the diff doesn’t demonstrate an existing test that should have been updated but wasn’t.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent skip of unknown usernames in add_members (admin/groups_controller.rb) is untested, regressing coverage removed with the old PATCH flow ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' / 'removing non-members')

adjudication.rationale: In the old spec, the incremental PATCH flow explicitly tested silent handling of invalid usernames ("succeeds silently when adding non-existent users") and removing users who aren’t members ("succeeds silently when removing non-members"). In the new implementation, `add_members` still silently ignores unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), and `remove_member` will also effectively succeed even if the user isn’t a member (`group.users.delete(user_id)`), but the updated specs shown no longer include equivalent coverage—only success cases for adding valid users and prohibition on automatic groups. This is a verifiable coverage regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group rename for non-automatic (custom) groups lost its test coverage — only rename-ignored-for-automatic-groups is tested

adjudication.rationale: In the controller spec, the prior update test verified renaming a non-automatic group (`xhr :put, :update, id: group.id, name: 'fred', ...` and `group.name.should == 'fred'`). In the new diff, the `.update` context only tests that name changes are ignored for an automatic group (`group = Group.find(1); group.name.should_not == 'WAT'`), and there is no remaining test that a custom (non-automatic) group can be renamed successfully. This is a concrete loss of test coverage visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update action does not strip group name while create does — inconsistent name-validation behavior unverified by tests

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create, the name is explicitly stripped: `group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`. In Admin::GroupsController#update, the name is assigned directly without stripping: `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic`. This is a concrete inconsistency introduced/visible in the diff. The spec adds a test ensuring stripping on create, but there is no corresponding test for update behavior, so the inconsistent name-normalization on update is unverified by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change of rename payload shape from params[:group] to top-level params has no corresponding test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change Admin::GroupsController#create and #update from expecting nested params (params[:group][:name], etc.) to top-level params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]). The updated specs do exercise the new top-level shape in a limited way (e.g., create strips spaces via `xhr :post, :create, name: " bob "` and update on an automatic group via `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, name: "WAT"`). So it’s not accurate to say there is *no* test coverage for the new payload shape. There is, however, no longer an explicit test that a non-automatic group can be renamed via the new top-level params, but that’s a test-gap/process concern rather than a verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member specs never assert that group.user_count is updated after membership changes, risking silent pagination breakage if the counter cache or Group#recalculate hook doesn't fire on the new mutation pattern (group.users.delete + save)
refresh_automatic_groups spec only verifies a mocked class method call and would stay green even if refresh_automatic_groups! were a no-op or broken — needs a real behavioral assertion

adjudication.rationale: In the updated spec under context ".refresh_automatic_groups", the test sets `Group.expects(:refresh_automatic_groups!).returns(true)` and then only asserts `response.status.should == 200`. In the controller, `refresh_automatic_groups` always calls `Group.refresh_automatic_groups!` and then unconditionally `render json: success_json`, so the test will pass as long as the method is invoked, even if the method’s implementation is a no-op or otherwise fails to actually refresh groups (but doesn’t raise). Thus the finding correctly identifies that the spec lacks a behavioral assertion beyond the mocked call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Automatic-group tests hardcode id: 1 instead of fabricating an explicit automatic group, making them fail for the wrong reason if seeding changes

adjudication.rationale: In the updated controller spec, multiple examples assume an automatic group exists with a fixed primary key of `1` (e.g., `xhr :put, :update, id: 1...` followed by `Group.find(1)`, and `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1...`). In the diff shown, these tests do not fabricate or otherwise set up an automatic group with `id=1`, so they rely on implicit seed/fixture state. That makes the tests brittle and can cause failures unrelated to the behavior under test if the seeded automatic group IDs change or if the test DB isn’t seeded the same way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member 'cannot remove members' test dispatches with xhr :put while the real route is DELETE, so the actual route wiring (delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member') is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin endpoint for removing a member is explicitly wired as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. However, in the added spec section `context ".remove_member"`, the test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` (visible at the bottom of the diff). In Rails controller specs this will invoke the controller action directly and will not exercise the DELETE route wiring, so the test both uses the wrong verb and fails to validate the actual routing/HTTP contract intended by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create error branch (render_json_error on duplicate/invalid group name) has no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#create`, the new implementation has an explicit failure path: `if group.save ... else render_json_error group end`. The updated spec adds a `.create` context but only covers the successful case (stripping spaces and creating "bob"); it does not exercise any invalid/duplicate name scenario that would hit `render_json_error`. Therefore the error branch is not covered by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member of a user who isn't a member (silent no-op) is untested, unlike the old PATCH flow which covered this case

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the old PATCH-based membership-change tests that explicitly covered the case “succeeds silently when removing non-members”. The new controller flow introduces a separate `remove_member` action (`group.users.delete(user_id)`), but in the updated spec file there is no replacement test asserting that removing a non-member is a no-op/success. So compared to the previous behavior, that scenario is now untested in the new flow, which is a verifiable test coverage regression present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members against a nonexistent group_id raising RecordNotFound (404) is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `add_members` which does `Group.find(params.require(:group_id).to_i)`. If `group_id` does not exist, Rails will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, which is typically handled by the framework/app as a 404. The proposed finding is about missing test coverage for that edge case, not a concrete defect introduced by the diff. The absence of a spec asserting the 404 behavior is not, by itself, a verifiable correctness/security bug in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Substantially rewritten frontend code (controller pagination actions, removeMember with bootbox confirm, addMembers, model findMembers, changed asJSON payload shape) has no JS tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows substantial frontend changes (new pagination actions, member add/remove UI, and Group#findMembers returning meta/members), but it does not establish any expectation or requirement that corresponding JavaScript tests must exist or be updated. The absence of added JS test files in this diff is not, by itself, a concrete defect introduced by the code change and is not verifiable as a correctness/security bug from the diff alone (especially since the project may not have a JS test suite in this area).

adjudication_records.issue_text: asJSON no longer wraps payload in {group: {...}} — a client/server contract change pinned only by server specs, vulnerable to undetected drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally changes the client/server payload shape and updates both sides to match. `group.js` `asJSON()` now returns a flat object (`{name, alias_level, visible}`) and `create()`/`save()` send that directly. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` were changed to read `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]` (no longer `params[:group]`). The updated specs also reflect the new parameter structure (e.g., `xhr :post, :create, name: " bob "`). So this is not an unpinned/undetected contract drift problem introduced by the diff; it’s a coordinated API change. The claim about being “pinned only by server specs” is speculative and not a verifiable defect in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers controller action has a known in-code-documented bug (TODO: should clear the input) where repeated clicks re-submit the same usernames, with no test documenting the behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` but never clears/resets the `usernames` property afterward, and it even contains an explicit comment `// TODO: should clear the input`. As a result, the input remains populated and repeated clicks will re-submit the same usernames string. No tests in the diff cover this client-side behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member bypasses model callbacks by using group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the domain method group.remove(user), leaving a stale denormalized user_count column in the groups table after every member removal
New specs only assert group.users.count and will not catch user_count drift caused by remove_member's raw association surgery
remove_member couples the controller to association internals, violating the separation of concerns the controller refactor was meant to enforce

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `remove_member` action in `Admin::GroupsController` does directly call `group.users.delete(user_id)`, but the proposed finding is an architectural/cleanliness critique (“couples the controller to association internals / separation of concerns”) rather than a concrete, verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff establishes a required abstraction (e.g., a `Group#remove` method that must be used for correctness), and this controller-level association manipulation does not, on its face, break behavior. Therefore it’s not a “real problem” under the criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1) produces a phantom extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 (when user_count != 0). If user_count is an exact multiple of limit, this yields an extra page (e.g., user_count=100, limit=50 => floor(2)+1=3, but only 2 pages exist). This also aligns with next() allowing offset to reach user_count, making currentPage compute to an out-of-range page number. Using Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (and/or clamping offset) avoids the phantom page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: showingLast doesn't engage on the real last page, leaving 'next' enabled and navigating to an offset equal to user_count, rendering an empty member list with correct-looking pagination
Offset clamp in group.js findMembers should be user_count - limit, not user_count, allowing out-of-range offsets
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point to the same pagination bug: clamping the next offset to `user_count` can yield an offset equal to the total, producing an empty last page. The candidate proposes clamping to `user_count - limit` instead, which directly prevents that empty-page scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips typo'd or nonexistent usernames while still returning 200 success_json with no indication of which users were added vs ignored

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the controller does `usernames.split(",").each` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; nonexistent/typo’d usernames are simply skipped with no error or reporting. After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if successful, responds with `render json: success_json`, so the client receives a 200-style success response without any indication of which usernames were ignored or whether zero users were actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The addMembers client does not clear the input after submission, so stale input invites re-clicks that 'succeed' again with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and currently only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `usernames` afterward. Since the template binds the `user-selector` directly to `usernames`, the entered value will remain after submission unless some external component logic clears it (not shown in this diff). This is a verifiable UX defect present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In group_member.hbs, the automatic property resolves to undefined inside the itemView (whose context is the item, not the group controller), so the remove link is shown for members of automatic groups

Clicking the remove link on an automatic group member fires removeMember which the server rejects with 422, leaving a delete control that silently does nothing; the guard should test the group (e.g., a canRemove property or binding against controller/model scope)
Offset clamping logic (Math.min/max against limit/user_count) is duplicated between the admin-group controller and the group model and should live in one place, the model

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce duplicated offset-boundary calculations: the admin controller’s `next`/`previous` actions compute offset with `Math.min/Math.max`, and the model’s `findMembers` also clamps `offset` (`Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))`). However, this is a maintainability/DRY refactor suggestion, not a verifiable correctness, security, or functional defect introduced by the diff. The code still works with duplication, and the finding does not point to a concrete bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 calls model.findMembers() and discards the promise with no error handling, so AJAX failures leave the members pane silently empty instead of aborting entry or surfacing errors

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. The diff removes the previous `afterModel` hooks that returned `model.findMembers()` (allowing the route to wait on the promise and letting rejections propagate through the route’s promise chain) and replaces them with bare calls in `setupController`:
- `admin_group_route.js`: `model.findMembers();`
- `group-members.js.es6`: `model.findMembers();`
In both cases the returned AJAX promise is discarded and there is no `.catch`/error handling. If the request fails, nothing in these routes will surface the failure or block/abort entry; the templates now render `members` (`{{each member in members}}`, `{{#each m in members}}`) which will remain unset/empty on failure, producing a silently empty members pane.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The .remove_member spec issues xhr :put while the route maps delete 'members' to groups#remove_member, so the spec no longer verifies the routing contract and a regression in config/routes.rb would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups member-removal endpoint is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, but in the updated controller spec under `context ".remove_member"` the test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` (visible in the diff). Rails controller specs invoking `:remove_member` directly don’t exercise routing, so this mismatch means the spec no longer reflects the actual HTTP contract and would not catch a regression/mismatch in routing/verb expectations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The add_members 422 spec only matches the route by luck because it also uses put instead of the correct verb

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups membership endpoint is explicitly defined as `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` (and `delete "members"` for remove). The spec in `groups_controller_spec.rb` correctly uses `xhr :put, :add_members, ...`, so it is not using the “wrong” verb, nor is it matching “by luck.” Also, controller specs invoke the action directly; they don’t depend on route matching in the first place.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members: server defaults limit to 50 for all groups but public group/members.hbs template got no pagination UI, so groups with more than 50 members show only the first 50 to regular users with no indication members are missing

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `GroupsController#members`, the endpoint now always applies pagination with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and returns only `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. On the public group members page, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets the controller model to the group and simply calls `model.findMembers()` (no limit/offset passed, so it uses the default 50/0), and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, which will display only `model.members` populated by `findMembers()`. Unlike the admin template (`admin/templates/group.hbs`) which adds next/previous pagination UI and updates `offset`, the public template shows no pagination controls or indication of total pages. Therefore groups with >50 members will show only the first 50 with no way for regular users to access the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation (Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1): with 100 members and limit 50, totalPages is 3 but only 2 pages exist, letting the admin navigate to an empty page; should use Math.ceil

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). This overcounts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3 instead of 2; 50/50 => 2 instead of 1). The template uses `{{currentPage}}/{{totalPages}}` and `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, so on the real last page (page 2 in the 100/50 case) `showingLast` will be false and the `next` action will allow advancing. `next` sets `offset` up to `user_count`, and `findMembers` then requests `offset=user_count`, which the server will return as an empty `members` list. So this is a real off-by-one bug introduced in the diff; `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with zero handled) would be correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale-offset cascade: findMembers clamps offset against the in-memory (stale) user_count, so after add/remove the UI can show an impossible page state (e.g. '2/1') with an empty list, requiring the user to click 'previous' to recover

Pagination race: next/previous optimistically mutate model.offset then fire async requests with no sequencing, cancellation, or failure handling; out-of-order responses mean the last response wins and the displayed list/counter can mismatch what the user requested

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, the `next`/`previous` actions immediately mutate `group.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()`, which performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and, on completion, unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response. There is no request sequencing, cancellation, or "latest request wins" guard. If a user clicks next/previous multiple times quickly, multiple overlapping XHRs can resolve out of order, and an older response will overwrite `members` and `offset` with stale `result.meta.offset`, causing the UI (member list and computed `currentPage`/`showingFirst`/`showingLast`) to reflect a different page than the most recent user action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members endpoint succeeds silently on unknown or untrimmed usernames (e.g. 'alice, bob' with leading space): failed lookups are skipped and the endpoint still returns 200/success with no partial-failure reporting about which usernames were not added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code takes `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and iterates `usernames.split(",")` without trimming each entry. It then does `User.find_by_username(username)` and only adds if found; missing users (including those with leading/trailing spaces like " bob") are silently skipped. Regardless of whether any users were actually added, it returns `success_json` (HTTP 200) as long as `group.save` succeeds, with no reporting of which usernames failed. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.
